claims.finding: On the evening of 2026-09-01, hours before this before-the-open print, CollPlant announced a 1-for-10 reverse share split to take effect at the Nasdaq open on 2026-09-04 - the session immediately AFTER the print - explicitly 'as part of the Company's strategic plan to regain compliance with the Nasdaq minimum bid price requirement for continued listing'.
claims.corpus_ref: docs/ee32750e276846aba37596bed7e3b23135338ee9.txt (snapshots/20260902T150801Z.json item 1); the underlying filing is filings.json/snapshot accession 0001213900-26-096233, form 6-K accepted 2026-09-01T20:30:01Z
claims.why_not_priced: Announced after the close on the eve of the release, into a corpus with zero news-search coverage (n_queries=0 in every sweep) and a Stocktwits stream that had already moved on to other tickers - only two of six captured messages that evening even mention it. Sandwiching a compliance reverse split between a pivot acquisition and a results print is a disclosure sequence no aggregator assembles, and a compliance-driven reverse split is a statement that the company does not expect the market to lift the price on its own. If it were priced, the stock would not have been bid 25% higher two sessions earlier on a pivot headline.
claims.independence: A second, independent Stocktwits participant reads the same sequence the same way the same evening - 'merger and they hav to r/s and er tomorrow this all adds up to a big pile of shit salad' - docs/ee32750e276846aba37596bed7e3b23135338ee9.txt

claims.finding: Two sessions before the print, on 2026-08-31, CollPlant announced it was acquiring LightSolver and entering the photonic-computing and supercomputing markets - consideration paid in newly issued shares AND warrants - and the stock traded 182,733,300 shares against a float the corpus puts at 13.0-13.5m, halted up, ran roughly 35% intraday, and closed only 8.4% higher before giving it all back over the next two sessions.
claims.corpus_ref: snapshots/20260831T150738Z.json item 2 (6-K accession 0001213900-26-095458, accepted 2026-08-31T10:07:51Z); docs/5135d7c19b08a747e07fe6779eb96726eb106de8.txt; quote.json bars 2026-08-27 through 2026-09-02
claims.why_not_priced: The announcement is public, so the headline is priced; the unaggregated part is the shape of the flow. 182.7m shares against a 13m float is roughly fourteen turns of the entire float in one session with the close only 8.4% up and a full round-trip within two days - that is distribution into retail, not accumulation. Nothing in the corpus computes that ratio, and there is no sell-side coverage of this name at all. A regenerative-medicine issuer buying a photonic-computing company for paper, two days before releasing results, is the same reframing-before-bad-numbers pattern.
claims.independence: filings.json shows the issuance machinery that makes the paper consideration credible as dilution rather than as strategy: F-1 (2026-03-30), F-1/A, 424B3 (2026-04-21 and 2026-07-17), F-3 (2026-01-09 and 2026-07-09), 424B5 (2026-02-06) and two Form Ds (2026-02-17, 2026-07-20) - https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1631487/000121390026095458/ea0303994-6k_collplant.htm

claims.finding: Three SCHEDULE 13D/A amendments were filed in twenty-five days - 2026-07-27, 2026-07-31 and 2026-08-21 - in a company whose float the corpus puts at 13.0-13.5m shares, immediately after a Form D private placement (2026-07-20) and a resale prospectus going effective (424B3, 2026-07-17).
claims.why_not_priced: 13D/A bodies are not stored and nothing in the capture references them. Three amendments in under a month at a sub-$50m issuer means a >5% holder's position is moving materially while a resale shelf is live - a supply fact with no publisher.
claims.independence: none - this rests on the same EDGAR index as finding 2 and should be collapsed into that source cluster.
